metadata.title: The issue of test-taking motivation in low- and high-stakes tests: are students underachieving in PISA?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for Sweden linked to Swedish grade 9 national registry data. The analytic sample is restricted to students with linked PISA and national test grade information (5432 available after consent; final analyses use N=4919 in Model 2/3 with 10 plausible values). Complex survey design features are handled via design-based standard error correction in Mplus using TYPE=COMPLEX with CLUSTER, and student final weights (W_FSTUWT) are applied to correct for unequal sampling probabilities and non-response. Missing PISA achievement data are handled via FIML within the SEM framework, while the paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a random sample of 5504 Swedish 15-year-olds who took PISA 2018. Students were linked to Swedish grade 9 national test registry data using personal identification numbers; 5432 students (98.7%) provided consent for linkage, and analyses report N=4919 for the main SEM models. The national test grade used is the reading subtest only (NT_Read), and PISA achievement outcomes are the reading domain scores based on 10 plausible values. Missingness in the national test grade is attributed to students absent on the testing day (10.6%), and missing responses on the PISA effort items range from 13.4% to 14.1%; missing achievement data are handled via FIML in Mplus.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Grade 9 Reading (Sweden) with linked Grade 9 national reading test
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Grade 9 Reading (Sweden) data linked to the Grade 9 national reading test, the study leveraged Test-taking effort (TTE) and National test grade (reading) to predict PISA reading achievement (plausible values), finding that TTE had a significant positive association with PISA scores even after controlling for NT_Read and that the TTE×NT_Read interaction was positive and statistically significant (b=3.73, β=0.05, p<.001). This indicates that low test-taking effort in low-stakes PISA can lead to underestimation of students’ true ability as reflected by high-stakes national performance, implying that effort monitoring and interpretation guidance are important for fair cross-student and cross-time comparisons, though the design is cross-sectional and cannot establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: The study links Swedish PISA 2018 reading outcomes (Grade 9; PISA reading achievement scored via 10 plausible values) with students’ grade 9 national reading test grades (high-stakes proxy for ability) and uses a latent-variable moderation framework to test whether self-reported test-taking effort (PISA TTE) predicts PISA performance beyond ability. In the main model, NT_Read strongly predicts PISA reading achievement (β=0.65, p<.001), while TTE shows a weaker but significant positive effect after controlling for NT_Read (β=0.15, p<.001). The moderation is statistically significant: the interaction TTE×NT_Read is positive (b=3.73, β=0.05, p<.001), with a small effect size (f2=0.005) and a modest R2 increase from 0.443 to 0.446. The paper applies student final weights (W_FSTUWT) and uses FIML for missingness, but it is not an ML predictive-modeling study and causal claims are limited by the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported effort.
